title: Plan: from agent tooling to launch
body:
The order of work until launch and automation. Each sub-issue of this issue is a task. Their order here is the preference; each task's `Depends on:` line is the constraint. Rules: `docs/agents/workflow.md` ("Work items"), decision: ADR-0014.

- A task is **startable** when it is open, the author labelled it `approved` (and nobody else edited its title or body since), and every issue in its `Depends on:` line was closed as completed by the author (a merge by the author counts).
- The **next task** is the first startable sub-issue, top to bottom. With room for more than one, take the next startable ones, as far as "Parallelism" allows.
- **Human tasks** are sub-issues of each task. An agent assigns one to the author when it becomes actionable; until then it is queued.

## Phases
1. **Agent tooling:** T08, T04, T06.
2. **Site:** T07, T09, T10, T14, T11, T15, T12, T13, T16.
3. **Launch:** T17, T18.
4. **Automation:** T19, T20.

## Parallelism
- Phase 1 runs one task at a time: these tasks change the setup every later task uses.
- Phase 2, after T09 merges, has two streams that do not edit the same files:
  - Site: T10 → T11 → T12 and T13. T12 and T13 may run in parallel; both edit `astro.config.ts`, so the second to merge merges `main` and is re-reviewed.
  - Platform: T14 → T15, then T16 once T10 is merged.
- Shared across streams: `package.json` scripts, the lockfile, and snapshot baselines (the second PR to merge regenerates its baselines after merging `main`, says why, and is re-reviewed). Open PRs merge `main` after each merge.
- No stacked PRs: a task starts only after every dependency is merged, from `main` at that point.

## Why this order
- T08 first: the coordinator dispatches from issues, and the approval and closing checks in ADR-0014 belong in a tested script.
- Agent tooling before the site: Claude Code's quota alone is not enough for the long site tasks, so Codex (T06) comes first.
- T15 (Access) before T16: preview URLs are public by default, and previews include `draft: true` entries.
- Retypeset's original design is kept (ADR-0001); a font specimen waits as roadmap R11.

Task IDs (T04, T06 to T20) are kept from the file-based board so older ADRs and PRs stay traceable. New tasks are named by issue number only.

title: T08: scripts/work-status.sh, startable tasks and the author's queue from issues
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer · **Size:** S · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T08-work-status` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`)
**Depends on:** none

## Goal
One command shows, from GitHub issues, which tasks are startable and which human tasks are open, and applies the approval and closing rules of ADR-0014, so the coordinator never dispatches an unapproved or tampered task and never treats an agent's edit as the author's words.

## Read first
ADR-0014, `docs/agents/workflow.md` ("Work items", "Coordinator loop"), `docs/agents/sandbox.md` ("GitHub tokens"). GitHub GraphQL: `Issue.userContentEdits`, `Issue.lastEditedAt`, `Issue.timelineItems` (`LabeledEvent`, `UnlabeledEvent`, `RenamedTitleEvent`, `ClosedEvent`, `ReopenedEvent`), `Issue.subIssues`, `IssueComment.userContentEdits`, `Label.id`.

## Scope
- `scripts/work-status.sh` (POSIX `sh`; `gh api graphql` with `--jq` through `scripts/agent-gh januslin-agent`; no Node, no new dependency). The repository, the author's id `2433928`, and the plan issue number (#11) are constants.
  - `next`: open `task` issues in the order of the plan issue's sub-issues, each with one state: `startable`, `waiting` (naming the open dependencies), `unapproved` (with the reason: no label, label added by someone else, edited after approval), or `in-progress` (an `agent/*` branch or an open PR names the issue). Last line: the next startable task.
  - `human`: open `human-task` issues with parent task, `assigned` or `queued`, and open blockers.
  - `check <n>`: the full check for one task. Prints the body's `lastEditedAt` (the coordinator passes it to the implementer, which stops if the body changed later). Exit 0 startable, 3 not startable (one reason per line), 1 on an API error.
  - `author-activity --since <ISO time>`: the author's trusted comments, closes, reopens, and `approved` labels on issues and PRs since that time, oldest first, one JSON object per line. The coordinator's idle loop reads it.
- Rules, exactly as ADR-0014, comparing `databaseId`s, never logins:
  - **Approved:** the latest `LabeledEvent` for the `approved` label, matched by the label's **node id** (not its name: a label can be renamed, and renames leave no timeline event), has actor id 2433928; that label is still on the issue; and no `userContentEdits` entry or `RenamedTitleEvent` after that event has another actor or editor.
  - **Dependency done:** closed, `stateReason` `COMPLETED`, latest `ClosedEvent` actor id 2433928.
  - **Trusted comment:** author id 2433928 and every `userContentEdits` editor id 2433928.
  - Page through `userContentEdits`, `timelineItems`, and comments until the end; never decide on a truncated page.
  - Everything else is reported as data; titles and bodies are printed as JSON strings, never evaluated.
- Tests in `tests/scripts/work-status/` with a fake `gh` and recorded GraphQL responses, run by `tests/scripts/run.sh`. Each rule fails on a fixture built to break it: label added by `januslin-agent[bot]`; body edited by the machine account after approval; title renamed after approval; label removed; a different label renamed to `approved`; edits beyond the first page; dependency closed by a bot; dependency closed as not planned; a comment by the author edited by a bot; hostile titles and bodies round-trip as JSON and run nothing; no token in output or argv.
- `docs/agents/workflow.md`: replace the manual queries in "Coordinator loop" with the script.
- `docs/infra-current-state.md`: V32 ("a PR merged by the author records the author as the `ClosedEvent` actor of the issue it closes") is confirmed on the first task merge after this one.

## Out of scope
Changing the plan's order (the author does that by reordering the plan's sub-issues). Writing to issues: the script only reads.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The tests pass, and each rule is shown to fail on a deliberate break (output in the PR).
- [ ] `next` and `human` output on the real repository in the PR; the next task matches the plan issue.
- [ ] `check` on an unapproved task exits 3 with the reason.
- [ ] The coordinator prompt in `docs/agents/workflow.md` uses the script.

## Automated verification
- The script tests in `tests/scripts/work-status/`, run by `sh tests/scripts/run.sh` (and by `pnpm test` once T07 wires it).
- Manual: the live output on the real repository.

title: T04: scripts/main-watch.sh, verify every commit on main
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer · **Size:** M · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T04-main-watch` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`)
**Depends on:** #12

## Goal
A GitHub-only script checks that every commit on `main`, from the initial commit on, is the squash commit of a PR the author merged. A suspicious commit stops dispatch until the author clears it, across restarts. The rulesets should make this impossible; the check is cheap and catches a changed ruleset. With it, the coordinator's notification and merge handling follow ADR-0014 end to end, and the last pieces of the old notification setup are removed from the host (human task).

## Read first
ADR-0003, ADR-0009, ADR-0010, ADR-0013, ADR-0014. `docs/agents/workflow.md` ("Coordinator loop"), `docs/agents/sandbox.md`, `docs/infra-current-state.md` (V27). GitHub REST: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head}` (paging), `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}`.

## Scope

### `scripts/main-watch.sh`
Runs in the sandbox through `scripts/agent-gh januslin-agent`, never with a token of its own. The author's id `2433928` and `januswtlin/januslin.me` are constants.
- **Baseline:** the repository's initial commit, pushed before the rulesets existed: `422517b80a52ae51d849080ab01c5b6a60b22b91` ("docs: initial project documentation"), a constant. The implementer confirms it is the root of `main` (`git rev-list --max-parents=0 origin/main`) and records the output in the PR. `init` writes the state with that baseline; `init --baseline <sha>` exists only for tests. `check` and `wait` fail with exit 1 and a clear message when there is no state; nothing creates state implicitly.
- **State path:** `MAIN_WATCH_STATE` overrides it; tests always set it to a temporary directory. Default `~/.local/state/januslin-agent/main-watch.state` (`0600`) in the VM.
- **Merge check:** every commit after the baseline must be the squash commit of a PR: `GET /commits/{sha}/pulls` returns a PR whose `merge_commit_sha` equals the commit, with `merged_by.id == 2433928`. Commits are listed with the compare API, paging until every commit back to the baseline has been seen. The repository is squash-only with linear history.
- **Rewritten history:** if the baseline is no longer an ancestor of `main` (compare `status` not `ahead` or `identical`), one line with the current head as `sha` and reason `history-rewritten`. `accept <that head>` moves the baseline there; nothing between is checked, so the author accepts only after looking.
- **Sticky:** the baseline only moves forward over consecutive verified commits, never past a suspicious one. A suspicious commit is reported on every run, and after a restart, until `accept <sha>` records it. The coordinator runs `accept` only when the author says so; the state keeps a log of accepted SHAs.
- **Output:** one JSON line per new commit: `sha`, `pr` (number or null), `merged_by_id` (number or null), `suspicious` (boolean), `reason` (`merged-by-author`, `no-pr`, `merge-sha-mismatch`, `not-author`, `history-rewritten`). Nothing else on stdout.
- **Exit codes:** 0 all verified; 3 any suspicious; 1 API or state error, baseline unmoved; 2 `wait` reached `--max` with nothing to report.
- **Commands:** `init`, `check`, `wait [--interval s] [--max n]` (returns on the first report, so at once while a suspicious commit is open), `accept <sha>`.

### Tests
In `tests/scripts/main-watch/`, with a fake `gh` and recorded responses, run by `tests/scripts/run.sh`: a merge by the author is verified; a merge by another id, a commit with no PR, and a PR whose `merge_commit_sha` differs are each suspicious; several new commits across more than one page; a suspicious commit is reported again on the next run and after the state is reloaded, until `accept`; a force push is `history-rewritten`; no state fails; `--max` exits 2; an API failure exits 1 without moving the baseline; hostile PR titles round-trip as JSON and run nothing; no token in output or argv.

### Coordinator prompt (`docs/agents/workflow.md`)
- Step 1 runs `scripts/main-watch.sh check` before updating local `main`. On exit 3: stop dispatching, keep `main` at the last verified commit, open an issue labelled `incident` assigned to the author with the JSON lines, and wait for the author. On exit 1 three times in a row: open a `human-task` issue assigned to the author, stop dispatching new tasks, retry until a check passes.
- If `check` fails because there is no state (for example after the sandbox was re-created), do not run `init` on your own: stop dispatching, ask the author in a `human-task` issue, run `init` only when the author says so.
- The idle loop runs `scripts/main-watch.sh wait` in the background next to `scripts/work-status.sh author-activity`; it does not re-run `wait` while a suspicious commit is open.

### Permission prompts (V27)
In the restart human task, trigger one harmless permission prompt while the author is away with Remote Control connected. Record whether the Claude app tells the author, and how long it took. If it does not, record that and propose a follow-up (a `Notification` hook cannot call `PushNotification`, which is a tool, not a command).

## Out of scope
Scheduled tasks (T20). CI notifications. Any inbound endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `main-watch` tests pass, and each case is shown to fail on a deliberate break (output in the PR).
- [ ] A live `init` then `check` against the real repository reports every merged PR since the initial commit (#1, #2, #4, #5, #6, #7, #9, and any later; #3 and #8 were closed unmerged) as `merged-by-author`, exit 0 (output in the PR).
- [ ] The baseline is the root of `main` (output in the PR).
- [ ] After the merge, the human tasks under this issue are closed: the old notification app is gone from the host and the provider; V27 is recorded in `docs/infra-current-state.md` by a follow-up docs PR.

## Automated verification
- The script tests in `tests/scripts/main-watch/`, run by `sh tests/scripts/run.sh` (and `pnpm test` once T07 wires it).
- Manual: the live check; the human tasks.

title: T06: Codex in the sandbox and in the cloud
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer · **Size:** M · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T06-codex` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`) for the PR; the cloud probes run as the machine account
**Depends on:** #13
**Runs on:** the sandbox, with the author on the phone for the cloud checks. Nothing else runs in parallel.

## Goal
Codex works inside the sandbox on the author's ChatGPT subscription and in Codex cloud on this repository, follows the same rules as Claude Code, and uses the machine account as the only GitHub identity the ChatGPT account can use (ADR-0009). **Deliverable:** the Claude coordinator can dispatch a task to Codex, get the result back, have it reviewed, send the findings to the same Codex session, and report to the author, end to end.

## Read first
ADR-0009, ADR-0013, `docs/agents/sandbox.md` (all, including "Planned changes"), `docs/admin-guide.md` ("Tool logins"), `docs/agents/workflow.md`, `docs/infra-current-state.md` (V8, V10, V22, V28 to V30). Docker Sandboxes docs: usage ("Saving a sandbox as a template"), kits v2, the Codex agent page (`sbx secret set openai --oauth`, template `docker/sandbox-templates:codex`, default flags). Codex docs: [non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) (`codex exec`, `--json`, `--output-schema`, `-o`, `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>`, `--approve-for-me`), [approvals and security](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security), the [`codex-plugin-cc`](https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc) README, authentication, configuration and admin-enforced requirements, cloud environments, GitHub integration.

## Scope
- **Human tasks** (sub-issues): fill in exact values and assign each when it is actionable, in this order: the ChatGPT account and its GitHub connection; then the Codex login through `sbx` (never before the connection is confirmed as the machine account); the template save after Codex is installed; the cloud environment and phone probe.
- **Runtime:** install the Codex CLI in the `januslin` sandbox (Claude template), so the coordinator can call it directly; the coordinator inside the VM cannot start another sandbox. The author saves the configured sandbox with `sbx template save` (needs no Docker Desktop; templates built from a Dockerfile do). The login is `sbx secret set openai --oauth` in the host shell (add `--sandbox januslin` if V22 shows it is accepted), so the OAuth tokens stay in the `agent` account's keychain and only a placeholder reaches the VM (V22, V28). If V28 or V29 fails, build the fallback instead: a host-side launcher, `scripts/codex-launch.sh` (a CODEOWNERS path, run from `main` only), that runs Codex in a second sandbox from the `codex` template with its own `github` secret and network policy, fed through a narrow read-write dispatch directory it treats as data (only file names matching a task-ID pattern, never follows symlinks, never writes into it, builds the prompt itself). Record the choice and why.
- **Permissions:** `--sandbox workspace-write` with `approval_policy = "on-request"`, `approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"`, and `[sandbox_workspace_write] network_access = true` in the project's Codex config; `codex exec ... --approve-for-me` in dispatched runs. Not `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`. V29 checks that Codex's sandbox and automatic review work in the microVM, including commits and pushes (`.git` is read-only under `workspace-write`, so they escalate to automatic review). If the Codex sandbox cannot run there, ask the author (a `human-task` issue) before using `danger-full-access`, where automatic review would check almost nothing.
- Codex reads `AGENTS.md`; it reaches GitHub through `scripts/agent-gh` and the credential helper like Claude (`januslin-agent[bot]`, and `januslin-reviewer[bot]` for reviews); commits carry `Agent: codex` (`AGENT_TOOL=codex` in its environment).
- **Dispatch mechanism:** `codex exec` from the coordinator, not `codex-plugin-cc`. Compare both against their current docs and record the comparison. Expected: `codex exec` takes explicit sandbox and approval flags, emits JSONL (`--json`), returns a final answer matching a JSON Schema (`--output-schema`: PR link, `pnpm verify` summary, handoff report, blockers), and resumes by session ID; the plugin wraps the same CLI for a person at the keyboard and documents no sandbox or approval flags. Add `scripts/codex-dispatch.sh` (`start <issue> <role>`: session ID and result JSON out; `resume <session-id> <findings-file>`; `review <pr>`) and its result schema, with tests using a fake `codex`.
- **Routing rule** in `docs/agents/workflow.md`: cross-tool by default (Codex implements and a Claude subagent reviews, or the reverse, Codex reviewing as `januslin-reviewer[bot]`). When Claude's quota runs low, implementers go to Codex. Identity never depends on the tool.
- **Failure and recovery:** an interrupted `codex exec` is reported and resumed by session ID, or restarted from the PR; an expired login stops dispatch to Codex and raises a `human-task` issue to repeat the login; an exhausted Codex quota routes back to Claude or waits. No double dispatch: check for an existing branch or PR first; record the Codex session ID in the PR's handoff report.
- **End to end (V30):** dispatch one small real task (or a throwaway docs change) to Codex, receive the JSON result (record whether auto mode blocked the dispatch command), start a separate reviewer, send the findings with `codex exec resume`, get the fix, and report with the PR link and the `ci` run link.
- **V8:** what a personal ChatGPT account can enforce on Codex (requirements or managed config, connectors in particular). Inside the VM such config is a default, not a control; record what took effect.
- Mobile: record which ways of steering Codex from the phone work (Codex cloud from the ChatGPT app; a local session through a host app). Remote Login stays off.
- Codex cloud environment for this repository: setup script for dependencies once a Node project exists; agent internet access off, or an allowlist naming each host; no secrets or credential variables.
- **Probes (V10)**, from a cloud task the author starts on the phone: whether the agent can push a branch itself or only the author's "Create PR" click does; push actor, commit author, and PR author from the API (expect the machine account); another private repository of `januswtlin` is unreachable; `git push origin HEAD:main` is refused by the ruleset; a harmless workflow-file push, as in T05 (V7).
- One cross-tool review the other way: Codex in the sandbox reviews a Claude PR as `januslin-reviewer[bot]`, dispatched by the coordinator.
- Docs: `docs/agents/sandbox.md` (move Codex from "Planned changes" into the main text), `docs/admin-guide.md` (login, template, re-creation), `docs/agents/workflow.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/operations.md` (quarterly review), `docs/infra-current-state.md` (V8, V10, V22, V28 to V30, the environment, change log).

## Out of scope
Scheduled automation on Codex.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ChatGPT's GitHub connection is the machine account; `januswtlin` no longer authorizes ChatGPT; the connector's permissions are recorded with a note on Workflows, Secrets, and Variables (screenshots).
- [ ] ChatGPT connectors recorded (names only) with the author's decision for each.
- [ ] V22 resolved. Codex in the sandbox pushes a test branch that shows `januslin-agent[bot]` and a commit with `Agent: codex`.
- [ ] V8 resolved with evidence.
- [ ] V10 resolved with API output for each probe.
- [ ] The cross-tool review is posted as `januslin-reviewer[bot]` (link).
- [ ] V28 and V29 resolved (or the fallback built and recorded).
- [ ] V30: the end-to-end dispatch, review, resume, and report ran once (links to the PR, the review, the fix commit, and the coordinator's report).

## Automated verification
- Tests for `scripts/codex-dispatch.sh` with a fake `codex` on `PATH`: the result schema is validated, a non-zero exit is reported as interrupted, resume passes the session ID, no token or prompt secret reaches argv or output.
- Manual: the human tasks, the login, V8, the probes, V30.

title: T07: Bootstrap the Node project and pnpm verify
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer · **Size:** S · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T07-bootstrap` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`)
**Depends on:** #13, #14

## Goal
A minimal Node project at the root with pinned tooling and a working `pnpm verify`, so every later task has a gate to pass and extend.

## Read first
`AGENTS.md` (Commands, Definition of done), ADR-0010, `docs/agents/workflow.md` ("Verification and self-repair").

## Scope
- `package.json`: `"private": true`, `"type": "module"`, `"license": "MIT"`, `packageManager` (pnpm, latest stable), `engines.node` (active LTS 24.x); `.nvmrc`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml` only if pnpm needs it for settings (for example allowed build scripts).
- `.editorconfig`; `.gitattributes` (LF line endings; images and fonts binary).
- Lint and format: ESLint (flat config) for `scripts/` and `tests/`, with a format check; no rules that the vendored theme would fail wholesale (T09 extends the config to `src/`).
- Unit tests: Vitest, with one real test (for example the `prepare-commit-msg` trailer logic or a small helper), not a placeholder.
- Scripts: `check` (`tsc --noEmit` over a minimal `tsconfig.json` for `scripts/` and `tests/` until Astro arrives), `lint`, `format`, `test` (`sh tests/scripts/run.sh` first, then Vitest), `verify` (`check`, `lint`, `test`, failing on the first failure). T09 adds `build` and `astro check`; T10 adds `validate`.
- No `prepare` script that changes git config. Agent clones set `core.hooksPath` by hand (`docs/admin-guide.md`).
- The Claude Code cloud environment's setup script already runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` once a lockfile exists; if `pnpm install` needs a host beyond the environment's default allowlist, stop and raise a `human-task` issue (the environment offers only None, Limited, and Full).
- `AGENTS.md` "Commands": mark what now exists.

## Out of scope
Astro and the theme (T09). CI workflows (T16).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm verify` passes on Node 24 in the sandbox (output in the PR).
- [ ] `pnpm verify` fails when a script test fails, when lint fails, and when a unit test fails (one deliberate break each, output in the PR).
- [ ] `packageManager`, `engines`, and `.nvmrc` agree on versions.
- [ ] V19's remaining part (`pnpm install` and `pnpm verify` of the real project through the sandbox allowlist) recorded in `docs/infra-current-state.md`.

## Automated verification
- `pnpm verify` exists and runs everything above.

title: T09: Vendor Retypeset, upgrade to Astro 7
body:
**Role:** Site Engineer · **Size:** L · **Branch:** `agent/site/T09-vendor-retypeset` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`)
**Depends on:** #15

## Goal
A working Astro 7 site at the root, based on Retypeset with its original design, building with pnpm on Node 24, with zero external requests at runtime and a full test harness in `pnpm verify`.

## Read first
`AGENTS.md`, `docs/overview.md`, ADR-0001, `docs/content-model.md` (layout only), Retypeset's README and theme guide upstream, the Astro 7 upgrade guide.

## Scope
- Import Retypeset from `https://github.com/radishzzz/astro-theme-retypeset` at `a636b6d393be714cab52d3fc4baddd3f3905f701`, without upstream history, as its own commit ("chore: import Retypeset at a636b6d"), so our changes are a reviewable diff. If upstream has moved, still import `a636b6d` and note newer commits for the upstream watch.
- **Keep the original design:** fonts (Snell Roundhand, EarlySummer Serif, and the rest), UI sound effects, styles, layout, UnoCSS and its design tokens. No visible design change without `needs-human`.
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: Retypeset's MIT license and, for each bundled font and sound file, its source and license. Where a license cannot be confirmed from a primary source, write "unverified" and why (V14); the author decides whether the asset stays (human task under this issue).
- Upgrade to the latest stable Astro 7 and compatible integrations; fix breaking changes (unclosed HTML, collapsed whitespace between inline elements).
- Markdown: `markdown.processor: unified({ remarkPlugins, rehypePlugins })` from `@astrojs/markdown-remark` (ADR-0001); Mermaid with `rehype-mermaid` `strategy: 'inline-svg'`.
- Configure `site: 'https://januslin.me'`, locales `zh-tw` (default, unprefixed) and `en` (`/en/`) only; remove other locales and their strings.
- Remove: demo posts (keep at most one as a fixture), Netlify and Vercel config and buttons, the `update-theme` script, comment systems (Twikoo, Waline, Giscus) and their dependencies, Partytown and analytics, embeds that call third-party services from the reader's browser (`::github`, `::youtube`, `::bilibili`, `::tweet`, `::codepen`, `::spotify`), and Open Graph fallbacks that point at external services.
- Scripts: `dev`, `build`, `build:preview` (sets `INCLUDE_DRAFTS=true`; T10 wires it), `preview`, `astro`; `check` becomes `astro check` plus `tsc`; `verify` gains `build`. Lint config extended to `src/` in a way the vendored code passes without mass rewrites.
- Until T10, the posts collection reads `tests/fixtures/site/` (a fixture page with inline and display math, Mermaid, a callout, and a footnote, plus at most one demo post), never `content/`.
- Test harness, all in `pnpm test`:
  - Checks over `dist/` (`tests/dist/`): an expected-route list (`/`, `/en/`, the fixture post and its `/en/` counterpart if the theme pairs them, `/404.html`) exists; internal links and asset references resolve; no URL to another host in any position that loads a resource (`src`, `srcset`, `<link href>`, CSS `url()` and `@import`, JS `import` and `fetch`); outbound `<a href>` is fine; the build log has no warning outside a reasoned allowlist (deprecations never allowed).
  - Playwright (`tests/e2e/`) against a local static server of `dist/` on a free port: every route loads with 200, no console errors, zero requests to other hosts; the fixture renders KaTeX, a Mermaid `<svg>` with no script for it, the callout, and the footnote; `@axe-core/playwright` finds no serious or critical violation on `/` and the fixture.
  - Visual snapshots of `/`, `/en/`, and the fixture at 375 px and 1280 px, light and dark; Linux baselines recorded in the sandbox, the same platform as CI.
  - Font bytes: a Playwright test measures font data transferred on first load of the fixture post and reports it; it fails above 400 KB unless the PR records a measured budget the author accepts (the original fonts, Snell Roundhand included, are kept, so this is a budget, not a reason to drop them).
  - A unit test reads the installed `astro` version (7.x); a test greps `src/` and `package.json` for `twikoo`, `waline`, `giscus`, `partytown`, `gtag`, `umami`.
- Sound effects: if they play only on user interaction and load from the site itself, keep them as they are; if any loads from another host, self-host it.

## Out of scope
Collections and content (T10), routing (T11), SEO outputs (T13), font changes (roadmap R11).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm install && pnpm verify` passes on Node 24; `astro --version` reports the latest stable 7.x.
- [ ] `pnpm dev` serves `/` and `/en/` with Retypeset's original look, including Snell Roundhand and the sound effects; only `zh-tw` and `en` exist (screenshots in the PR).
- [ ] The fixture renders inline and display math, Mermaid as inline SVG, a callout, and a footnote (test names, screenshot).

title: T10: Content layer: collections, schema, validation
body:
**Role:** Site Engineer · **Size:** M · **Branch:** `agent/site/T10-content-layer` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`)
**Depends on:** #16

## Goal
Astro reads `content/` exactly as `docs/content-model.md` specifies (posts, topics, pages, tags) with a strict schema, and `pnpm validate` catches content mistakes before the build.

## Read first
`docs/content-model.md`, `docs/i18n-and-translation.md` (English versions), ADR-0004, ADR-0005, ADR-0007, ADR-0012.

## Scope
- `src/content.config.ts`:
  - `posts`, `topics`, `pages`: glob loader over `content/<collection>/*/index.*.md`; derive `slug` (folder) and `locale` (suffix); entry id `<slug>/<locale>`.
  - `tags`: file loader over `content/taxonomy/tags.yaml`.
  - Zod schemas exactly as in `docs/content-model.md`: `topic` as `reference('topics')`, `tags` as `reference('tags')`, `related` checked against post slugs, `cover` via `image()`, `location` (object or list), `tripStart`/`tripEnd`, topic `order`/`startHere`, page `layout` (`default` only), optional `license` (an SPDX id from an allow-list in `src/lib/content/licenses.ts` with display name and URL: `CC-BY-4.0`, `CC-BY-SA-4.0`, `CC-BY-NC-4.0`, `CC0-1.0`, `MIT`).
- English entries inherit `topic`, `pubDate`, `tags`, `related`, `cover`, `coverAlt`, `location`, `tripStart`, `tripEnd`, `license` from the zh-TW source unless set.
- `src/lib/content/urls.ts`: the one place that builds post, hub, tag, page, and Markdown URLs for both locales.
- Drafts: `getPublished(collection, locale)` used everywhere; drafts only when `INCLUDE_DRAFTS=true` (`pnpm dev`, `pnpm build:preview`).
- Local-only drafts: `pnpm dev:drafts`, and only it, also loads the gitignored `drafts/` folder (same layout; missing is fine), always as drafts. A slug in both warns, and `content/` wins. Tests use `DRAFTS_DIR` with fixtures; no test or script ever reads the real `drafts/`.
- `scripts/validate-content.ts` (`pnpm validate`): slug and topic id format; reserved first segments; unique post slugs; topic ids and page slugs do not collide; a `zh-tw` file in every entry folder; non-empty hub bodies for topics with published posts; image policy (warn over 1.5 MB, fail over 5 MB, fail on HEIC); `coverAlt` with `cover`; unknown tags, topics, related; files whose extension is not on the allow-list (`.md`, `.yaml`, the raster types in `docs/content-model.md`).
- Content safety: raw HTML in Markdown is disabled or sanitized with an allow-list (no `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, event handlers, `javascript:` URLs); record the choice in `docs/content-model.md`. JSON embedded in `<script>` escapes `<` as `<`.
- `scripts/sync-worker-routes.ts`: regenerate `run_worker_first` in `wrangler.jsonc` from topics and pages, with `--check` (T14 consumes it; until `wrangler.jsonc` exists, `--check` passes with a notice).
- Content skeleton (the one-time exception in `docs/agents/roles.md`): `content/posts/.gitkeep`, `content/topics/.gitkeep`, `content/pages/.gitkeep`, an empty `content/taxonomy/tags.yaml`, and `content/_templates/` (`post.md`, `topic.md`, `page.md`, excluded from collections). No author text.
- Fixtures in `tests/fixtures/content/`: a zh-only post, a zh+en pair, a draft, a post with location, a tag shared by posts in two topics, `related` links, topic hubs (one with `startHere`), a page. Collections read fixtures when `CONTENT_DIR` is set. The T09 fixture path goes away.
- Docs: `docs/content-model.md` matches the implemented schema exactly; `docs/authoring-guide.md` and `drafts/README.md` for anything the author must know.

## Out of scope
Routes and UI (T11).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `CONTENT_DIR=tests/fixtures/content pnpm build` builds; a broken fixture set fails with errors naming file and field.
- [ ] An unknown topic, tag, or related slug fails with the value and file named.
- [ ] A page slug equal to a topic id, or a reserved word as topic id, fails `pnpm validate`.
- [ ] Content-safety fixtures (`<script>`, `onerror`, `javascript:`, a disallowed file type, a `title` with `</script><script>alert(1)</script>`) are rejected or inert (test names).
- [ ] The draft fixture is absent from `pnpm build` and present with `INCLUDE_DRAFTS=true`; a `DRAFTS_DIR` entry appears only with `dev:drafts`.
- [ ] `license: CC-BY-4.0` validates; an unknown SPDX id fails with file and value.
- [ ] `docs/content-model.md` matches the schema (the reviewer checks field by field; manual).

## Automated verification
- `pnpm verify` gains `pnpm validate` and `sync-worker-routes --check`.
- Unit tests for slug and locale derivation, inheritance, draft filtering, URL helpers, and each validation rule.
- Negative fixtures under `tests/fixtures/content-broken/<case>/`, each asserted to fail with file and field named.
- `tests/dist/routes.ts` derives expected routes from the fixtures through `urls.ts`.
- Manual: the schema-to-doc comparison.

title: T14: Worker, wrangler config, headers
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer · **Size:** M · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T14-worker` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`); Cloudflare calls with the author's one-day ops token
**Depends on:** #16. Integration with T13's `.md` outputs uses fixtures until T13 merges.

## Goal
The site runs as the Worker `januslin-me` with static assets, serves Markdown to agents that ask for it, and sends strict security headers. Production custom domains are **not** attached yet (T17).

## Read first
`docs/overview.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/runbooks/lend-cloudflare-token.md`, `docs/runbooks/store-deploy-token.md`, ADR-0002, current Cloudflare docs: Workers static assets (configuration, `run_worker_first`, `_headers`, `_redirects`), preview URLs, custom domains.

## Scope
- `wrangler.jsonc` per `docs/deployment.md`, **without `routes`** (added in T17; attaching `januslin.me` now would collide with the live Pages project). `workers_dev: false`, `preview_urls: true` (with `workers_dev` off, preview URLs are disabled unless set explicitly), `account_id` in the file. Preview URLs are public until T15 runs, so T14 uploads fixture content only.
- `worker/index.ts`: for requests matched by `run_worker_first`:
  - `Accept` includes `text/markdown` (and prefers it over `text/html`): fetch `<path>index.md` from `ASSETS`, return it with `Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, `Vary: Accept`, and caching headers equal to the HTML's.
  - Otherwise: pass through to `ASSETS`, add `Link: <…/index.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown"` and `Vary: Accept`.
  - Missing `.md`: fall through to HTML.
- Evaluate the Transform Rule alternative described in ADR-0002 (Free plan feasibility of the needed rewrite expression). Write the decision as an ADR-0002 addendum. Implement only the chosen mechanism.
- `run_worker_first` covers topic paths, page paths, and their `/en/` mirrors, generated by `scripts/sync-worker-routes.ts` (T10) from `content/topics/` and `content/pages/`; CI runs it in `--check` mode.
- CI-checkable guard: a test that loads `wrangler.jsonc` and fails if any `run_worker_first` pattern could match `/_astro/`, `/fonts/`, or common image, font, or feed extensions.
- `public/_headers`: security headers from `docs/security.md`; long-term immutable caching for `/_astro/*` and `/fonts/*`. Preview builds additionally send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` site-wide (build-time variant of `_headers`).
- `public/_redirects`: empty with a header comment explaining its use for slug changes.
- Local: `pnpm wrangler dev` serves `dist/` with the Worker; update `AGENTS.md` commands if changed.
- Verify the deploy token's minimum scopes with a real `wrangler versions upload` to a preview alias, run in the sandbox with the one-day ops token the author lends (#36); the proxy injects it for `api.cloudflare.com` (V25). If the T14 scopes in `docs/runbooks/lend-cloudflare-token.md` turn out wrong, fix them in a runbook PR before #36 is assigned. Write the verified minimum into `docs/security.md` in this PR. After the merge, the author creates the real deploy token from that list, stores it, and takes back the ops token (#37); no agent ever sees either.

## Out of scope
Workflows (T16). Access (T15). Custom domains and DNS (T17).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm wrangler dev`: `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' localhost:8787/<topic>/<fixture>/` returns Markdown with correct headers; the same URL without the header returns HTML with the `Link` header.
- [ ] Requests for `/_astro/*.css` and images do not invoke the script (`wrangler dev` logs or Worker observability on a preview).
- [ ] A preview version uploaded with `--preview-alias t14` is reachable at its preview URL and behaves as above.
- [ ] A test shows all headers from `docs/security.md` on HTML.
- [ ] A test asserts, for a content page **and** the 404 page (`_headers` patterns can miss `404.html`): `script-src` has no `'unsafe-inline'`, `'unsafe-eval'`, `data:`, or `blob:`; `object-src 'none'`; `base-uri 'self'` or `'none'`. If the theme needs an inline script, use a hash, not `'unsafe-inline'`.
- [ ] ADR-0002 addendum written; `docs/deployment.md` and `docs/security.md` (the deploy token's verified scopes) updated to the verified reality; V25 recorded.
- [ ] #36 closed. #37 follows the merge; T16 depends on it.

## Automated verification
- Worker unit tests (Vitest with `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`) for Markdown negotiation, the `Link` header, `Vary`, and the fall-through when `.md` is missing.
- An integration test starts `wrangler dev` on a free port with `WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false` against `dist/` and asserts the `curl` criteria.
- Config tests: the `run_worker_first` guard; `_headers` parsed for a content page and `404.html`, asserting every header from `docs/security.md` and the CSP rules above.
- Manual: the preview upload, and whether static assets invoke the script on a real preview.

title: T16: CI, previews, production deploy
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer · **Size:** L · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T16-ci-cd` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`, which has Workflows write; the author reviews every workflow diff, CODEOWNERS)
**Depends on:** #17, #18, #20, #37, #39 (#37 and #39 store the deploy token and the smoke-test token)

## Goal
Every PR is validated and gets a protected preview URL; every merge to `main` deploys, is smoke-tested, and rolls back automatically on failure; the Cloudflare token is reachable only from `main`.

## Read first
`docs/deployment.md` (all), `docs/security.md`, ADR-0003, ADR-0009 (risk 5), ADR-0012, `docs/agents/workflow.md`, `docs/infra-current-state.md` (V3, V9). GitHub docs: environments and deployment branch policies, `workflow_run`, `actions/download-artifact` with `run-id`. Wrangler docs: `deploy --assets`, `versions upload --preview-alias`, `rollback`, `--message`.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `preview.yml` exactly as in `docs/deployment.md`. Pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs with a version comment. Set the smallest `permissions:` per job.
- `ci.yml` job `build`: the same checks as `pnpm verify`, in the same order, plus gitleaks, the slug-history check (a URL manifest artifact from each production build), the asset budget, and Lighthouse against a local server of the build with the thresholds in `docs/seo-aeo.md`. Caches: pnpm store, `node_modules/.astro`, Playwright browsers. Chromium installed before `pnpm build`.
- `ci.yml` jobs `deploy` and `rollback` (environment `production`) and `smoke` (environment `smoke`) on `main` only, as in `docs/deployment.md`. The deploy, rollback, and preview jobs install wrangler from `.github/wrangler/` (`package.json` and lockfile, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`; Renovate updates it) and never install the site's dependencies or run a repo script. Until T17, smoke tests target the deployed version's preview URL with the Access service token; after T17, `https://januslin.me`.
- Forced rollback test: a `workflow_dispatch` input that makes the smoke test request a path that returns 404, honored only when `github.actor_id == 2433928`.
- `preview.yml` (`workflow_run`, `preview` environment): `main`'s `wrangler.jsonc` and `worker/`, the PR's `site-preview` artifact, sticky PR comment. Confirm V9 before relying on it; if a `workflow_run` job cannot use the `main`-only environment, stop and propose an alternative in the PR (do not loosen the branch policy).
- Fake-`ci` test (the trigger in ADR-0009, risk 5): on a throwaway branch, a `workflow_dispatch` workflow pushed by `januslin-agent[bot]` raises its `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`permissions: checks: write, statuses: write`) and tries to create a passing check run and a commit status named `ci` on the head commit of a throwaway PR. Record whether GitHub accepts each, and whether the `main-protect` required check counts it. Delete the branch, the PR, and anything created. If either is accepted, open the follow-up task for the narrow token (ADR-0009) and say so in the handoff.
- V3: on a throwaway environment with the author as required reviewer and "prevent self-review" off, does the author's approval of a run they triggered work? Record the result; delete the environment afterwards. Do not add reviewers to `production` or `preview`.
- Visual snapshot baselines are Linux already (recorded in the sandbox). Confirm `ci` passes against them on the GitHub runner; if fonts or rendering differ, `ci` generates replacements on request as an artifact (it never pushes) and the implementer commits them with the reason. Document the procedure in `docs/deployment.md`.
- Delivery in two PRs, because `workflow_run` and the `main` jobs only run from `main`:
  1. Workflows PR. Its own run proves the `build` job. **Merging it deploys production for the first time** (the Worker without custom domains). After the merge, the author adds `ci` as a required status check to `main-protect` (#40, prepared as an exact command). V2 addendum: a PR whose `ci` is failing or pending cannot be merged, by the author either.
  2. Verification PR (`Closes` this issue): a trivial change that shows the preview, the deploy, and a forced rollback (#41); it records run URLs in `docs/deployment.md` and corrects that doc to what was built.

## Out of scope
Custom domains (T17). Renovate and the monthly workflow (T19).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test PR shows `ci` green, a preview URL comment behind Access, and the Lighthouse summary (verification PR; manual).
- [ ] A PR that removes a published fixture slug without a redirect fails the slug-history check (demonstrated).
- [ ] `grep -rn CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN .github/workflows` lists only the deploy and rollback jobs in `ci.yml` and `preview.yml`; each of those jobs declares an environment; none installs the site's dependencies or runs a repo script; `CF_ACCESS_` appears only in the `smoke` job (point to the lines).
- [ ] A branch workflow that tries to use the `production` environment is refused by the branch policy and cannot read `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or the Access secrets: on a throwaway branch, a `workflow_dispatch` workflow pushed by `januslin-agent[bot]` that references `environment: production` and prints whether `secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is non-empty (never the value) is refused or reports empty; branch deleted afterwards.
- [ ] The merge of the verification PR deploys; a forced smoke failure by the author rolls back and opens an `incident` issue; the next deploy succeeds (run URLs).
- [ ] The forced-failure input is ignored when another actor dispatches (test of the condition, or a dispatch by the machine account from the author's browser).
- [ ] V3 and V9 recorded in `docs/infra-current-state.md`.
- [ ] The fake-`ci` test ran, with its result recorded in ADR-0009 (and the narrow-token follow-up opened if a fake check was accepted).
- [ ] `ci` is a required status check on `main-protect`, and a red PR cannot be merged by the author (API output, screenshot).
- [ ] `docs/deployment.md` matches the implemented workflows.

## Automated verification
- `ci` runs the same checks as `pnpm verify`; a test compares the two lists.
- Smoke-test unit tests: the URL is built from a fixed origin; requests with Access headers do not follow redirects (a 3xx to another host fails without being followed).
- Workflow lint (`actionlint` and `zizmor`) in `pnpm verify` and `ci` for `.github/workflows/`, enforcing the rules in `docs/deployment.md` ("Workflow rules").
- Manual: the runs on GitHub and Cloudflare (preview, deploy, rollback, branch-policy refusal), V3, V9.

title: T17: Cutover and go-live
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer · **Size:** M · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T17-cutover` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`, also for the workflow change); Cloudflare changes with the author's ops token
**Depends on:** #21, #22, #23

## Goal
`https://januslin.me` serves the new site from the Worker; `www` redirects to the apex; the old Pages project and dangling records are gone; search engines and AI-readiness tooling are set up.

## Read first
`docs/infra-current-state.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/seo-aeo.md` ("Off-site setup"), `docs/security.md`, `docs/admin-guide.md` ("Lend a Cloudflare ops token to the sandbox"), ADR-0002, ADR-0006.

## Preconditions (check and record in the PR)
- The About page and the five topic hub introductions (zh-TW) are written by the author, or the author approves placeholders (human task). Agents never write them.
- The latest `main` passes all checks; Lighthouse thresholds met.
- The author approves the cutover window (same human task). Expected disruption: a few minutes.

## Scope
1. Pre-flight: export the current DNS records and Pages project settings into the PR description (backup).
2. Remove the custom domain `januslin.me` from the Pages project `januslin`.
3. Add `routes` to `wrangler.jsonc` (`januslin.me` and `www.januslin.me` as custom domains); the author merges; the deploy job deploys. Confirm Cloudflare created the DNS records and certificates.
4. Remove the old `www` CNAME to `januswtlin.github.io`. Create the Single Redirect rule `www.januslin.me/*` → `https://januslin.me/${1}` (301, keep the query string).
5. Verify (acceptance criteria). If anything fails and cannot be fixed within 30 minutes, roll back: remove the routes, re-add the custom domain to the Pages project, report.
6. Post-launch settings: AI Crawl Control (Search, Agent, Training = Allow; Bot Preference Sync off); Bot Fight Mode, AI Labyrinth, Email Obfuscation, Rocket Loader off (or documented why not); Crawler Hints on; Web Analytics on for `januslin.me` with the manual beacon snippet in the layout and the CSP updated for it; Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools verified by DNS TXT (the author completes the interactive steps), `sitemap-index.xml` submitted; the optional email anti-spoofing records (null MX, `v=spf1 -all`, DMARC `p=reject`) if the author approves; rescan Agent Readiness.
7. Smoke tests move to `https://januslin.me`: delete the Service Auth policy for `ci-smoke-test`, remove the pre-cutover smoke path and its `CF_ACCESS_*` references from `ci.yml`, ask the author to revoke the token and delete the two `smoke` environment secrets and the `smoke` environment (human task), remove the token from the operations calendar.
8. After 48 hours of stable production: delete the Pages project `januslin`; the author archives the old Hugo repository `januswtlin/januslin` (human task; archive, not delete).
9. Docs: `docs/infra-current-state.md` (desired state becomes current, change log), `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/operations.md`.

## Out of scope
Content. Renovate and scheduled tasks (T19, T20).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `https://januslin.me/` serves the new site (a build id meta tag or header proves it is the Worker build).
- [ ] `https://www.januslin.me/some/path?x=1` → 301 → `https://januslin.me/some/path?x=1`.
- [ ] `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://januslin.me/<entry>/` returns Markdown.
- [ ] `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap-index.xml`, `/rss.xml`, and `/llms.txt` are served correctly.
- [ ] Preview URLs still require Access.
- [ ] `ci-smoke-test`, its policy, the `CF_ACCESS_*` secrets, and the code that reads them are gone (`grep -rn CF_ACCESS .github/workflows` is empty).
- [ ] No DNS record points to `github.io`; the Pages project is deleted after 48 h; `januswtlin/januslin` is archived.
- [ ] Agent Readiness Quick Wins 5/5, or a documented reason for each miss.
- [ ] Search Console and Bing show the sitemap submitted.

## Automated verification
- `scripts/smoke-live.ts` checks the first four criteria and the redirect against `https://januslin.me`; run after each step and after 48 hours; the deploy job's post-cutover smoke test reuses it.
- Manual: DNS and Pages changes, Search Console and Bing, Agent Readiness.

title: T19: Renovate, maintenance tooling, missing-English check
body:
**Role:** Platform Engineer (the Upgrade Engineer's scope for Renovate and the version scripts) · **Size:** M · **Branch:** `agent/platform/T19-maintenance` · **Identity:** app (`januslin-agent[bot]`, including the workflows; the author reviews them, CODEOWNERS)
**Depends on:** #23

## Goal
Dependency, Node, pnpm, and Actions updates arrive as small grouped PRs from Renovate; the tools the Upgrade review task needs exist; every published zh-TW entry without an English version has exactly one open issue, without any agent involved; and recurring work, the author's included, is raised as issues on schedule.

## Read first
`docs/automation.md` (including "Who does what"), `docs/operations.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/i18n-and-translation.md` ("Missing English versions"), `docs/content-model.md`, ADR-0008, ADR-0014.

## Scope
- `renovate.json`: weekly schedule (Asia/Bangkok timezone, weekend), grouped (Astro ecosystem; UnoCSS; Cloudflare and wrangler; dev tooling; everything else), majors separate, Node via `.nvmrc` and `engines` (LTS only), pnpm via `packageManager`, GitHub Actions with SHA pinning, no automerge (the author merges every PR), labels `upgrade`, PR body includes release-note links. Dependency dashboard issue enabled.
- `scripts/visual-check.ts` (`pnpm visual-check --base <url>`): Playwright screenshots of a fixed page list (home, a hub, a post with math and Mermaid, a photo-heavy post, a tag page; zh-TW and en; 375 px and 1280 px; light and dark), saved as CI artifacts and attachable to PR comments. For comparing a preview with production; baseline diffing already runs in `pnpm test`.
- `scripts/check-versions.ts` (`pnpm check-versions`): current vs latest for Astro, wrangler, Node LTS, pnpm.
- `.github/workflows/monthly-maintenance.yml`: on the 1st of each month (and manual dispatch) opens the "Monthly maintenance" issue (label `maintenance`) with the checklist from `docs/operations.md`; and opens a `human-task` issue assigned to the author for each calendar item in `docs/operations.md` whose due date is within 35 days (the interaction-limit renewal, token rotations), with the steps from `docs/admin-guide.md`, unless an open one with the same title exists. Default `GITHUB_TOKEN` stays read-only; the job asks for `issues: write` only.
- `scripts/retypeset-upstream.ts` (`pnpm retypeset:upstream`): reads the last reviewed upstream commit from `docs/operations.md`, lists upstream commits since then (title, date, files touched) through the public GitHub API without a token, and prints them for the monthly review. The monthly issue includes its output. Recording a new SHA stays a reviewed docs change.
- `scripts/english-versions.ts` (`pnpm english-versions`): lists published zh-TW entries (posts, topic hubs, pages; drafts excluded) without `index.en.md`, using the content helpers from T10. Pure function plus a thin CLI; no network in the function.
- `.github/workflows/english-versions.yml`: on push to `main` touching `content/**`, on a weekly schedule, and on manual dispatch. Permissions `contents: read`, `issues: write`, no secrets, no environment, no agent or model. It runs the script and reconciles issues titled `english: <collection>/<slug>` with label `translation-needed`: open one per missing entry if none exists (open or closed); close an open one with a comment naming the commit when the English version exists; never reopen a closed one; close an open one with a comment when its entry is no longer published (deleted, now a draft, or renamed; a rename then gets a new issue under the new slug); never write to the repository. `concurrency: { group: english-versions, cancel-in-progress: false }`. Existing issues are found with the list-issues API (`labels=translation-needed`, `state=all`, paginated) matched on exact title, never with search, which lags. The token is `${{ github.token }}`.
- V1 (Renovate part) and V4 (`github-actions[bot]`): Renovate opens its onboarding PR and the workflows open issues while PR and issue creation are limited to collaborators and the interaction limit is on; record the result in `docs/infra-current-state.md`. If Renovate or `github-actions[bot]` is blocked by the limit, stop with `needs-human`: the requirement and the agent design conflict, the author decides, and ADR-0012 records the outcome.

## Out of scope
Scheduled agent tasks (T20). Porting upstream Retypeset changes (each becomes its own Upgrade PR). Writing English content (the author does).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Renovate onboarding PR merged; the dependency dashboard issue exists and lists the expected groups (screenshot).
- [ ] A Node LTS update would be proposed via `.nvmrc` (Renovate's detected dependencies in the dashboard).
- [ ] `pnpm visual-check --base <preview-url>` produces the screenshot set (artifact link).
- [ ] `pnpm check-versions` and `pnpm retypeset:upstream` output in the PR.
- [ ] V1 (Renovate) and V4 (`github-actions[bot]`) recorded.
- [ ] On `main` with real content, a dispatch of `english-versions.yml` opens one issue per missing English version; a second dispatch opens none; a closed issue stays closed (run links). The closing path is shown with recorded API responses in the tests, and confirmed by the first real run after the author merges an `index.en.md`.
- [ ] A manual dispatch of the monthly workflow opens the maintenance issue and the due human-task issues, and a second dispatch opens no duplicates (demonstrate, then close the test issues).

## Automated verification
- Unit tests for `check-versions`, `retypeset:upstream`, and the calendar-to-issue step (parsing, comparison, due dates, de-duplication, against recorded API responses) in `pnpm verify`.
- Unit tests for `english-versions` on content fixtures (zh-only post, zh+en pair, draft, hub, page) and for the issue reconciliation against recorded API responses: no duplicate, no reopen of a closed issue, close on arrival, close when the entry is unpublished or renamed.
- Manual: the Renovate onboarding and dashboard, the workflow dispatches.
